avis.titre: Reformulated and made it cheap and toxic
avis.texte: I have always used Clinique Liquid Facial Soap - dry combination - since I was in high school. This soap has been in my rotation and the only face soap I've successfully and consistently used for over two decades. But as two other reviewers mentioned - Clinique has reformulated this soap with cheap, toxic ingredients. They now included Citric Acid, which is a common preservative that is not in fact a product of citrus but a product of a lab grown MOLD, which couldn't possibly be safe for skin, and Methylchloroisothiazolinone & Methylisothiazolinone. The combination is banned in Europe - as they are known skin irritants, can cause organ toxicity, and are two of the most predominant contact allergens found in cosmetic products. For a company that claims to be "clean" - clearly that is not true. I am wildly disappointed, and am tired of seeing you cheapen and reformulate all of your products I and many others have used for years. I have been a lifetime shopper - but I won't be anymore. Clearly you only value profit as a corporation, and don't stand by your original principles.

I'm absolutely stunned and saddened that Clinique reformulated the Dry/Combo and Oily/Combo cleansers to contain Methylchloroisothiazolinone and Methylisothiazolinone. For a brand that is meant to cater to sensitive skin, these are honestly the worst ingredients they could have added to these classic formulas. I would have been happier with fragrance being added! This is a major reformulation that could cause reactions for many people!

avis.titre: Very poor replacement for the extra mild facial soap bar
avis.texte: I am very disappointed that Clinique discontinued the extra mild facial soap bar. And there are several reasons why I find the liquid facial soap an unsatisfactory substitute for the bar soap. But the primary reason is the deeply concerning use deeply concerning use of Methylchloroisothiazolinone and Methylisothiazolinone (aka MCI/MI). I strongly agree with another reviewer about the toxicity of these chemicals. The mixture of these two is chiefly used as a preservative in this product -- not as a benefit to the skin of the user. Although used in cosmetic applications (soap, shampoo, etc) it is also used for industrial applications and can be found in paints, moist toilet paper, metalworking fluids. It is proven in multiple studies here (including the NIH) and abroad to be a high allergen, with common symptoms of redness, swelling, hives, itching, and flaky skin. This combination is banned in Europe and several other countries. I have used Clinique products -- especially the bar soap, starting with type 3, then 2, then 1 -- for over 45 years. You have lost a customer for facial cleaning bars -- unless you bring back an extra mild facial soap bar.
